state.seed_assertion: Data controllers are required to carry out a DPIA before any processing that is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.

sentences.1: The measures and safeguards provided to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects under the GDPR;
sentences.2: Rights and freedoms of natural persons refer mainly to data protection and privacy, but also include other fundamental rights such as freedom of speech, freedom of thought, and freedom of movement.
sentences.3: The reference to the rights and freedoms of natural persons refers mainly to data protection and the protection of privacy but also, where appropriate, to other fundamental rights, such as freedom of speech, freedom of thought, freedom of movement, prohibition of discrimination, the right to freedom and freedom of conscience and religion.
sentences.4: Potential impacts on the rights and freedoms of data subjects are identified in case of events such as illegitimate access to data, an unwanted modification of data or their disappearance
sentences.5: A DPIA must assess the origin, nature, particularity and gravity of risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
sentences.6: The risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects are managed [article 35, paragraph 7, point c)]: The origin, the nature, the particularity and the gravity of the risks are assessed (recital 84)
sentences.7: A Data Protection Impact Assessment must be conducted when a type of processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.
sentences.8: Article 35(1) says that you must do a DPIA where a type of processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals
